thread:
emma: Heads-up — NovaHealth getting close to a reserved-capacity commit. Legal just flagged cross-region data residency needs (EU-only for PHI) and wants a clear ramp plan for expanding to US later. Need inputs on preheat budget, autoscale fallback, and pricing credits.
raj: Thanks. Can we get their traffic profile? qps, concurrency, percent tail during peak windows?
emma: Provided earlier: 95th qps ~ 200, typical burst to 1k qps for ~10–20m once/day, baseline steady 50 qps. Mostly chat generation with long contexts (~2k tokens) and some embeddings.
liam: For that burst shape with long context, recommend dedicated pool of 4x A100-class GPUs (reserved) with a small burst pool of 2x transient instances to handle spikes. KV warmup will be the hairy part for long contexts.
raj: Model selection? They plan to use a quantized LLM v2-large (8-bit) for cost. We'll need to validate throughput numbers.
liam: Agreed. Rough calc: with our quantized runtime, a single A100-equivalent gives ~120 qps for 2k context streaming generation (with batching). So 4 GPUs ~480 qps sustained; add 2 burst nodes for headroom. That covers 1k qps bursts if autoscale preheats.
simon: Legal asks about cross-region isolation. Ops note: we can pin EU traffic to EU-only pools and provision mirrored pools in US for later. But preheat for EU must not source data from US.
marta: On the compliance side — they'll need the security questionnaire answered about KMS, access controls, and CU processing location. Also want audit log retention policy. I can draft answers but need the precise retention SLA.
emma: They asked for a 12-month audit log retention with export ability. Is that standard?
liam: Our default retention for hosted is 90d; enterprise private can extend to 12 months with export. We'll flag a support ticket to enable export to their S3.
raj: Pricing question: if they commit to 4 reserved GPUs monthly, can we offer a preheat credit for burst usage? They want cost predictability.
emma: They're pushing for a 10% burst-credit pool and a flat egress + per-token during bursts.
simon: We typically do a reserved commit discount + burst credits purchased as option. For legal cross-region constraint, burst pool must be region-bound, so credits are per-region.
liam: Operationally, preheat plan: schedule a rolling KV warmup 30m before forecasted peak if they give us a daily window. Otherwise, use reactive warmup which adds latency. We can also persist checkpoints for common prefixes to speed recovery.
raj: Can we show synthetic load results for the quantized model with this context? Customer will want numbers for 99th p95/p99 latencies.
liam: I'll run a smoke sim tonight and upload results. Expect p95 token latency ~80–110ms range on quantized path. p99 might spike during cold KV.
emma: What about autoscale policy config — can we share a sample that fits their SLOs?
liam: Sample policy below. Feel free to copy to the POC playbook.

```yaml
# autoscale policy (example)
scale_target: reserved_pool
min_capacity: 4  # reserved GPUs
max_capacity: 6  # allows 2 burst nodes
scale_up_threshold_qps: 400
scale_down_threshold_qps: 250
preheat_window_minutes: 30
fallback_model: quantized-v2-small
eviction_policy: block-new-requests-when-queue>1000
```

liam: Notes: preheat_window_minutes requires an agreed daily ramp window or an API trigger from customer so we can pre-warm KV.
marta: For the contract, legal needs explicit language about region-bound burst and data placement guarantees. I'll prepare a clause: "All data processed under the EU residency option shall remain in EU-managed infrastructure and shall not be replicated to other regions without Customer's prior written consent."
simon: Also include a section on emergency failover: we can fail traffic to US if EU capacity is unhealthy, but only after customer sign-off and masked data options.
emma: NovaHealth asked about SLA for p95 latency during bursts. Realistic commitment?
liam: We can offer a p95 token latency SLA of 250ms during reserved capacity; bursts covered by credits but not SLA unless we preheat to full burst capacity.
raj: So commercial options: (A) reserve 4 GPUs + 10% burst credits, no SLA on burst; (B) reserve 6 GPUs (higher commit) with SLA; (C) dedicated private deploy with EU-only tenancy and extended log retention.
emma: I'll put those three options in the quote. Need cost delta for B vs A.
simon: Quick calc: option A cost = reserved(4) * monthly_rate - commit_discount + burst_credit_fee; option B adds 2 reserved GPUs (~+50% cost). I'll ask finance for exact numbers.
marta: Security questionnaire — I need the KMS key rotation cadence and attestation docs. Raj, can you attach the standard attestation and KMS rotation policy?
raj: Attestation doc attached in DM. KMS rotation is 90 days by default; we can support customer-managed keys in Private deploy.
liam: One more ops note: we should include a preheat runbook step in the POC: 1) confirm daily ramp window; 2) call POC preheat API with start time; 3) monitor KV fill metrics; 4) verify sample latency at p95/p99; 5) release burst nodes after window.
emma: Perfect. I'll consolidate into the POC checklist and send to NovaHealth legal + infra.
simon: @emma ping me if they push for automatic cross-region failover — that requires a separate review.
deploy-bot: deploy status: test-sim-run-4123 completed; results uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-poc-results/novahealth/4123456789/.
emma: Thanks all — action items: liam runs synthetic sim (ETA 24h), sim results to sales playbook; marta drafts contract clause and security answers (ETA 48h); sim + pricing numbers to NovaHealth by EOD +2.
raj: I'll prepare model perf baseline and attach to the quote.
liam: kicking off the test run now. will post raw numbers. :rocket:
